name: Minneapolis
tagline: City of Lakes, Arts Excellence, and Midwestern Value
description: Minneapolis punches well above its weight in culture, dining, and outdoor recreation. The Chain of Lakes, extensive bike trails, and one of the best park systems in the nation make it an outdoor lover's paradise — even in winter with cross-country skiing and ice fishing. The Twin Cities boast more theater seats per capita than anywhere outside New York, and the dining scene rivals cities twice its size. Housing is affordable by major metro standards, and while winters are brutal, the city has adapted with skyways and a resilient, community-oriented culture.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – safe in most neighborhoods; standard urban awareness needed
quickFacts.climate: Continental with cold, snowy winters and warm, humid summers

housing.description: Modest studio or small older 1BR in Uptown, Northeast, or Longfellow

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with occasional meals out

healthcare.description: MinnesotaCare (MN's Basic Health Program, MNsure) — VERIFIED as the top of the $0–80/mo sliding-scale band (avg ~$50), non-asset-tested, for MAGI held ≤ ~200% FPL (~$31,300); assumes an early retiree (45–55), older retirees should budget more. **Fallback (if MAGI can't be held that low): a subsidized MNsure Silver ~$450 (→ Lean total $2,400).** Above the 2026 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600) an unsubsidized MNsure Silver is only ~$530 here (verified age-50), far below the ~$1,000 typical of higher-cost states

transportation.description: Metro Transit monthly pass ($120) plus occasional winter rideshare (a modest paid-off car runs ~$250)

entertainment.description: The Chain of Lakes, riverfront trails, and low-key local outings

1M.lifestyle: A genuinely frugal Minneapolis life anchored by a modest studio or small older one-bedroom in Uptown, Northeast, or Longfellow, with home cooking the norm and the Metro Transit pass covering most trips. The defining advantage is health coverage — keeping income under roughly $31,300 qualifies for MinnesotaCare at well under $100 a month, a fraction of the typical US marketplace premium. Winter heating is a real line, but Minnesota's cheap natural gas and a small, well-insulated unit keep it contained. Leisure leans on the city's free assets: the lakes, the riverfront, and miles of park trails.

housing.description: Decent 1BR in walkable Uptown, Whittier, or Northeast

dining.description: Dining out a few times a week across the city's food scene

healthcare.description: Subsidized MNsure Silver at mid-range income, roughly equal to an unsubsidized low-cost Bronze

transportation.description: A reliable used car for year-round winter driving

entertainment.description: Breweries, live music, pro sports, and the lakefront

2M.lifestyle: A secure, comfortable routine built on a proper one-bedroom in a walkable district like Uptown, Whittier, or Northeast, with meals out a few times a week across the Twin Cities' strong food scene and a reliable car for winter mobility. Health coverage steps up to a subsidized MNsure Silver or an unsubsidized low-cost Bronze — the MinnesotaCare edge fades once income clears about 200% of poverty. Entertainment widens to breweries, live music, and pro sports on top of the free lakefront.

housing.description: Quality newer 1BR in Northeast, Uptown, or the North Loop edge

dining.description: Frequent quality dining across the metro

healthcare.description: Unsubsidized MNsure Silver above the 2026 ~$62,600 ACA cliff — still far below high-cost states thanks to Minnesota's low benchmark and reinsurance

transportation.description: A comfortable, reliable car for winter and regional trips

entertainment.description: Theater, concerts, sports, dining, and weekend travel

3M.lifestyle: A relaxed, financially-independent life in a quality newer one-bedroom in a desirable walkable neighborhood — Northeast's nicer buildings, Uptown, or the edge of the North Loop — dining out several times a week with a real travel budget. Health coverage is the swing variable: at a FIRE-level income above the 2026 ACA cliff the tax credits disappear, yet Minnesota's benchmark is so low that the unsubsidized Silver here (~$530) sits far under the ~$1,000 common in higher-cost states. A comfortable car handles the winters and regional driving.

housing.description: Luxury 1BR high-rise in the North Loop, Mill District, or by the lakes

dining.description: Near-daily dining at the city's best tables

healthcare.description: A full-price MNsure Gold plan minimizing out-of-pocket

entertainment.description: Premium leisure, events, and cultural memberships

5M.lifestyle: Upscale living in a luxury one-bedroom high-rise in the North Loop, Mill District, or near the lakes, with near-daily dining at the city's best tables, a nice car, and regular housekeeping. Health coverage is a full-price MNsure Gold plan chosen for low out-of-pocket rather than price. A generous travel-and-experiences budget rounds out an affluent, low-friction lifestyle.

housing.description: Penthouse or large luxury residence in the Mill District, North Loop, or near Lake of the Isles

dining.description: Private-chef-caliber dining and the finest restaurants

healthcare.description: Top-tier unsubsidized MNsure Gold plus concierge/direct primary care (below Cincinnati's ~$1,400, as MN's benchmark warrants)

transportation.description: Luxury cars and charters on demand

entertainment.description: A full cultural and social calendar, clubs, and travel

domesticHelp.description: Weekly housekeeping plus occasional additional help

luxuryExtras.description: Bespoke travel, club memberships, and luxury experiences

10M.lifestyle: The top of what Minneapolis rents at the very top of the market — a penthouse or large luxury residence in the Mill District, North Loop, or by Lake of the Isles, with private-chef-caliber and fine-restaurant dining, luxury cars with charters on demand, and regular domestic help. Health coverage is a top-tier unsubsidized Gold plan paired with concierge or direct primary care. Even at this ceiling Minnesota's premiums keep the health line below what the same tier costs in most US metros; the spend is defined by discretionary luxury, not necessity.
